read.body: Check four things: the goal, the files Droid plans to change, its approach, and how it will verify the result.

approve.title: 调整后再批准
approve.body: Comment on any line or choose Keep iterating if something is off. Approve once the plan matches what you want.

confirm.title: 接受 Spec
confirm.body: Pick how much Droid does without asking while it builds. Medium suits most tasks. Select Confirm to start.

specMode.definition: Droid researches your task and proposes a plan, called a spec, before it changes any code. While planning it only reads and searches: no file edits, commits, or services. Approve the spec to start building, or keep iterating on it.

autonomy.definition: Autonomy sets the highest-risk work Droid can run without pausing for approval. Higher levels let Droid do more on its own, and you can cycle levels as you work through a task.

firstSession.title: 你的首个 Session

connectTools.title: 连接工具
connectTools.summary: Give Droid context from your apps
connectTools.instructions: Connect the app where your work is tracked, such as Linear or Jira, then select Continue
connectTools.tip: Droid works from the same sources you do. Once Linear or Jira is connected, you can paste a ticket link and Droid reads the ticket before it writes a spec, so you skip explaining the task again. Connect the app where your work is tracked first; you can add Slack, Notion, or Google Drive later in Settings.

startSession.title: 启动 Spec Session
startSession.summary: Give Droid a clear task in Spec mode
startSession.instructions: Start a new session in a project, pick a model, switch to Spec mode, and send a task, or use the example below
startSession.folderInstructions: Start a new session in an empty folder, pick a model, switch to Spec mode, and send your task, or use the example below
startSession.tip: A clear task gets you a spec you can approve on the first pass. Name the outcome, where Droid should look, what it must not touch, and how you will check the result, or start from the example below. A vague task makes Droid guess, and you spend the review correcting its guesses.

giveTask.title: 审查并批准 Spec
giveTask.summary: Read the plan, steer it, and approve it
giveTask.instructions: Droid researches and writes a spec. Read it, comment on anything that is off, then select Approve Spec and Confirm
giveTask.tip: Fixing a plan takes one comment, while fixing code takes another run. Before you approve, check that the spec has the right goal, the files you expect, an approach you agree with, and a way to verify the result. If a part is wrong, comment on that line or choose Keep iterating, and Droid revises the spec.

verify.label: 验证方式

sampleTask.prompt: Find one small, important function in this repo that has no tests. Follow the existing test style and runner. Don’t change the function’s behavior or add dependencies. Run the tests and show me they pass.

taskTip.title: 请 Droid 编写有依据的 Spec
taskTip.body: Describe a feature idea. Droid reads the code, then plans a one-page spec for you to approve.

sampleTask.title: 根据当前代码编写 Spec
sampleTask.description: Droid writes one Markdown file and changes no code.
sampleTask.prompt: Write a one-page spec in docs/specs/ for a small feature idea I’ll describe next. Base “how it works today” on the actual code and link the files. Don’t change any code. End with open questions and 3 acceptance criteria I can test.

parts.outcome: A one-page spec in docs/specs/ for one feature idea.
parts.context: How it works today, from the actual code, with file links.
parts.verify: Open questions and 3 acceptance criteria you can test.

taskTip.title: 请 Droid 审查界面
taskTip.body: Name one screen. Droid checks it against your design system and plans the two worst fixes.

sampleTask.title: 按设计系统审查一个界面
sampleTask.description: A small, visual diff you can judge at a glance.
sampleTask.prompt: Audit one settings page for inconsistent spacing, colors, type, and empty, loading, and error states. Use our design tokens and components, not hardcoded values. Fix only the top two issues, no layout redesign. Show before and after screenshots.

parts.outcome: The top two consistency fixes on one settings page.
parts.constraints: No hardcoded values and no layout redesign.

taskTip.title: 请 Droid 编写客户简报
taskTip.body: Name the company and the meeting. Droid plans the brief and its sources for you to approve.

sampleTask.title: 准备客户简报
sampleTask.description: One page from public sources, with every fact linked.
sampleTask.prompt: Create account-brief.md for my next meeting with a company I’ll name. Use public sources, with links. Mark assumptions; no guesses presented as facts. End with 3 discovery questions and one sentence I could open with.

parts.constraints: Assumptions marked, no guesses presented as facts.
parts.verify: Every fact links to the source you can open.

taskTip.title: 请 Droid 编写发布文案
taskTip.body: Name the feature and the audience. Droid plans a one-pager grounded in your docs.

sampleTask.description: Short, sourced copy you can check claim by claim.
sampleTask.prompt: Write launch.md: a one-page announcement for a feature I’ll name, for our customers. Base it on our docs and changelog. No claims we can’t support, under 300 words. List every factual claim with its source at the end.

parts.outcome: launch.md, a one-page announcement for customers.
parts.constraints: Under 300 words, with no claims you cannot support.
parts.verify: Every claim listed with its source.

parts.verify: A flag on every number you did not give.

parts.outcome: notes-summary.md with decisions, actions, and questions.
parts.verify: Anything unclear is marked for you to check.

context.label: 上下文
context.description: Droid doesn’t know your conventions or what a task means, so it guesses. AGENTS.md, a README, and issue templates replace guesses with facts.

access.label: 访问能力
access.description: Droid can’t build or run your code, so it can’t see what it does. Documented builds, env templates, and logs open the door.

checks.label: 检查
checks.description: Nothing tells Droid it’s wrong until you do. Linters, tests, branch protection, and analytics catch mistakes before review.

half.prompt: Your repo passes half of all its checks. Which level is it?
half.explanation: 50% clears the 40% bar for Level 3, not the 60% for Level 4.

0.explanation: Level 2 starts at 20%. Half of all checks reaches higher.

2.explanation: Level 4 needs 60% of all checks, and you pass 50%.

cheapest.prompt: You have time for one fix: add AGENTS.md (Level 2) or set up tracing (Level 3). Which raises your score more?
cheapest.explanation: Every check counts the same, so do the faster fix first. AGENTS.md takes minutes.

agentsMd.label: AGENTS.md
agentsMd.explanation: It’s the faster fix, but it doesn’t count for more. Every check weighs the same.

tracing.label: 追踪
tracing.explanation: A higher-level check doesn’t count for more. Every check weighs the same.

runReadinessReport.instructions: In a new session in a Git project with an origin remote, send /readiness-report. It takes several minutes; the sidebar shows when it’s ready.
runReadinessReport.tip: The scorecard shows which checks your repo fails, so you fix real gaps instead of guessing. Droid looks for things like a README, a lint config, and pre-commit hooks, then saves the result to Agent Readiness. Large repos can take up to an hour, so start it now and keep going

runReadinessReport.title: 运行就绪度报告
runReadinessReport.body: Send /readiness-report, then come back to the lesson. Droid scores your repo on its own.

learnAgentReadiness.summary: Learn the three reasons agents stumble
learnAgentReadiness.instructions: When Droid struggles in a repo, it’s missing context, access, or checks. Open each to see which pillars your report grades.
learnAgentReadiness.tip: Knowing why Droid stumbles tells you which fix pays off. Without an AGENTS.md, Droid guesses your build and test commands and wastes turns; without tests or a linter, it can’t check its own work. Each pillar in your report traces back to one of these three causes

activity.heading: 代理为何遇到困难
activity.placeholder: 选择原因，查看可解决问题的维度。

climbReadinessLevels.summary: See how your level is set
climbReadinessLevels.instructions: Your level is the share of all checks you pass: 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% unlock Levels 2 to 5. Every check counts the same.
climbReadinessLevels.tip: Because every check counts the same, the cheapest failing checks are the fastest way up. Adding a lint config moves your score as much as setting up distributed tracing. Count how many checks stand between you and the next 20% band before you start a big project

reviewReadinessReport.summary: Read your level and weakest pillar
reviewReadinessReport.instructions: Find three things on your scorecard: your level, how far you are from the next one, and your weakest pillar.
reviewReadinessReport.tip: Your weakest pillar is where Droid wastes the most time in this repo, so it’s the best place to start. Open a failing check to read why it failed, such as no pre-commit hooks. Ask Droid about any check you don’t recognize before you fix it

askAboutReport.title: 询问报告内容

askAboutReport.example: Explain my readiness level simply and tell me what to fix first

skip.label: 不等待报告，继续学习
skip.note: Keep going or leave. The sidebar marks this lesson when your scorecard is ready, so come back to read it.

fixReadinessGap.summary: Have Droid fix one failing check
fixReadinessGap.instructions: Select Fix on a failing check and send the /readiness-fix it drafts. Then read what Droid changes.
fixReadinessGap.tip: One fix moves your score and shows you what a readiness change looks like. /readiness-fix names the failing check, so Droid changes only what that check needs instead of rewriting your setup. If you have no report yet, ask Droid to write an AGENTS.md, the highest-leverage fix in most repos

tourReadinessPage.instructions: Agent Readiness in Analytics tracks every scored repo and your organization’s level. Follow the tour.
tourReadinessPage.tip: {{tourPanelTipPrefix}} This page shows every scored repo, so you can spot which ones slow Droid down. After you merge a fix, refresh that repo to confirm the check now passes; your report appears here once Droid saves it.

startSession.summary: Ask Droid to review your changes
startSession.instructions: Start a new session in a project with uncommitted changes and send the tip’s example. In the CLI, /review does the same.
startSession.noComputerInstructions: Set up a computer, then start a session in a project with uncommitted changes and send: Review my uncommitted changes
startSession.tip: A review before you push catches bugs while the change is fresh and cheap to fix. Droid reads your diff and the code around it, and reports only bugs it can explain. If you have no uncommitted changes, ask Droid to review your last commit instead

askForCodeReview.title: 请求代码审查
askForCodeReview.body: Ask in plain words. Droid looks for real bugs, not style.

readCodeReview.summary: Learn the parts of a finding
readCodeReview.instructions: While Droid reviews, read this sample finding. Select each part, then find the highest priority in your own review.
readCodeReview.tip: Priority tells you what to fix before you merge and what can wait. P0 blocks the merge, P1 is a real bug Droid is confident about, P2 is plausible but unproven, and P3 is minor. A review with no findings is a good result

activity.heading: 一条审查发现

priority.label: 优先级
priority.note: P0 blocks the merge. P1 is a real bug Droid is confident about.

location.label: 位置
location.note: The file and line that break, with the code below.

impact.label: 影响
impact.note: What goes wrong for users. Droid skips style nitpicks.

fix.label: 修复
fix.note: A suggested fix you can ask Droid to apply.

activity.caption: Start with the highest priority. Fix P0 and P1 before you merge.

fixReviewFinding.summary: Have Droid fix the top finding
fixReviewFinding.instructions: Draft the fix below and send it. When Droid finishes, open Changes and check the fix and its test.
fixReviewFinding.tip: A test proves the fix works and fails if someone brings the bug back. In Changes, check that the test covers the exact case the finding describes. If Droid found nothing, ask it to add a test for your change instead

fixAndTest.title: 修复最高优先级发现
fixAndTest.description: A test shows it’s fixed and keeps it fixed.

action.text: Fix the highest-priority finding and add a test that catches it

learnDroidExec.summary: Run a review from a script or CI
learnDroidExec.instructions: droid exec runs one task with no chat, so a script or CI job can run it. Read the command a CI review would use.
learnDroidExec.tip: droid exec runs Droid in CI or a script with no one watching, so the --auto level is your safety net. With no flag it only reads; low allows file edits, medium adds installs and commits, and high allows git push. If a task needs more, it stops and keeps what it already changed

activity.heading: 通过 CI 审查并修复

autonomy.label: 自主级别
autonomy.note: With no --auto flag, Droid only reads. high also allows edits, commits, and git push.

where.label: 运行位置
where.note: A CI runner or a throwaway branch keeps a wrong change away from your main work.

learnPullRequestReview.instructions: Droid can review each pull request and comment on real bugs. Set it up from a session or from Automations, and add your rules.
learnPullRequestReview.tip: Automatic review checks every pull request, including the ones nobody asked about. Set review_depth: deep for thorough reviews or shallow for fast ones. Write your team’s rules in .factory/skills/review-guidelines/SKILL.md so Droid flags what your reviewers would

weekdaySummary.prompt: Summarize changed tickets every weekday at 9am.
weekdaySummary.explanation: A clock starts this run, so it’s Scheduled. Schedules run in UTC unless you name a time zone.

whyNot.slack: Nobody posts a message to start it. The time of day is the trigger.
whyNot.github: No repository event happens at 9am. Only the clock changes.
whyNot.webhook: No outside service calls in. The time of day is the trigger.

channelMessage.explanation: A message in a channel starts each run, and Droid replies in its thread.

whyNot.scheduled: A schedule would answer late and in batches. Each message should start its own run.
whyNot.github: The questions arrive in Slack, not in a repository.
whyNot.webhook: Slack is built in. A webhook is for services that have no trigger of their own.

externalAlert.prompt: Investigate each alert your monitoring tool sends.
externalAlert.explanation: The monitoring tool posts each alert to the automation’s webhook URL, which starts a run.

whyNot.scheduled: Polling on a schedule finds alerts late. A webhook starts a run as each one fires.
whyNot.slack: That works only if alerts land in Slack. Here the tool calls Factory directly.
whyNot.github: Alerts come from your monitoring tool, not from a repository.

droidSdk.sdkExample:
import asyncio, sys
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel
from droid_sdk import run

class Triage(BaseModel):
    summary: str
    severity: Literal["low", "medium", "high"]

bug_report = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
result = asyncio.run(run(f"Triage this bug report: {bug_report}", output=Triage))
if not result.success:
    raise SystemExit(result.subtype)
queue = "Priority" if result.output.severity == "high" else "Standard"
print(queue, result.output.summary)

action.text: In a new folder, sdk-practice, build and run a small Python script with the droid-sdk package. Give Droid this fictional bug: "Search crashes when the query is empty." Get a summary and severity (low, medium, high) as structured output; route high to Priority, the rest to Standard. Use my existing login. Run it and show the command, exit status and printed output.

In a new folder, sdk-practice, build and run a small Node script with @factory/droid-sdk. Give Droid this fictional bug: "Search crashes when the query is empty." An automation runs a prompt on a trigger with no code to own, while an SDK script lets your code check Droid’s answer and decide what happens next, such as where a bug is routed. learnDroidSdk.tip: Reading the script shows where Droid’s judgment ends and your rules begin. In Python, run(prompt, output=Triage) returns a result whose output matches your Pydantic model, and result.success and result.subtype tell you whether the run worked. The TypeScript SDK works the same way, with run() and an outputFormat JSON schema.

newBugs.explanation: New reports keep arriving, so a workstream can keep finding and fixing them.

whyNot.one-off: There’s no finish line: next week brings new reports. One session can’t watch for them.

oneBug.prompt: Fix the login bug in ticket APP-42.
oneBug.explanation: One known task with a clear finish line. A regular session is enough.

whyNot.ongoing: Nothing new will arrive once APP-42 is fixed. A workstream would sit idle.

flakyTests.prompt: Keep flaky tests from piling up in CI.
flakyTests.explanation: New flaky tests keep appearing, and each needs its own fix. That is ongoing work.

whyNot.one-off: Fixing today’s flaky tests won’t stop tomorrow’s. The goal needs repeated checks.

confirmProposal.prompt: During setup you select Confirm proposal. What happens next?

live.label: 工作流上线
live.explanation: Activation is a separate, later choice. Confirming only approves what Droid builds.

confirmProposal.explanation: Droid builds the agreed setup and runs a test. Nothing runs on its own yet.

testRun.prompt: The test run found real signals. Does it open pull requests?

opens.label: 会，每项变更一个
opens.explanation: A test run is a dry run. It never edits outside systems or opens PRs.

testRun.explanation: You judge the signals, changes, and one plan before anything touches your repos.

autoMerge.prompt: You activate the workstream. Will Droid merge its own PRs?

merges.label: 会，检查通过后合并
merges.explanation: Auto-merge starts off. You must turn it on, and it never skips required reviews.

autoMerge.explanation: Auto-merge starts off, and review gates start on. Doing work and merging are separate permissions.

workstreams.suggestOnly: Research only; don’t create or change anything.

learnWorkstreams.summary: Tell ongoing goals from one-off tasks
learnWorkstreams.instructions: A workstream is an ongoing goal Droid keeps working on: it finds new work, fixes it, and follows the PRs. Sort each example.
learnWorkstreams.tip: A workstream pays off when the same kind of work keeps arriving. A one-off ticket finishes faster in a normal session, while recurring bug reports or dependency bumps suit a workstream that picks up each new one. If you can’t name where the next item will come from, start with a session.

learnWorkstreamStages.summary: Trace one bug from report to merge
learnWorkstreamStages.instructions: Every workstream runs four stages. Tap each pin to follow two bug reports to one merged fix.
learnWorkstreamStages.tip: Knowing the four stages tells you where to look when work stalls. Intake polls your connected sources and records signals, Triage groups them into changes, Workers build each change, and Steward drives its pull request to green through merge or closure. The Software Factory overview maps your whole delivery lifecycle; a workstream is one pipeline inside it.

activity.heading: 一个缺陷，四个阶段

goal.text: Goal: fix login bugs customers report.

items.0: `#support`: “Login loops on Safari” becomes signal S-12.
items.1: `#support`: “Can’t sign in on Safari” becomes signal S-13.

triage.text: S-12 and S-13 become one change, C-4: “Fix the Safari redirect loop.”

items.0: Droid writes a spec for C-4.
items.2: Droid writes the code and opens pull request #481.

items.0: CI fails, so Droid pushes a fix.
items.1: CI goes green and the pull request merges.

intake.label: 接收
intake.note: Intake checks your sources and records each new item as a signal.

triage.label: 分流
triage.note: Triage groups related signals into one change you can approve or decline.

workers.label: 工作代理
workers.note: A worker writes a spec, waits for your approval, then builds and opens a pull request.

steward.label: 维护代理
steward.note: The steward drives the PR to green and records it merged or closed.

activity.caption: Signals come in, changes go out. You approve at each gate.

askWorkstreamGoal.summary: Ask Droid for goals that fit
askWorkstreamGoal.instructions: Start a new session in a project you know, or an empty folder. Pick a draft and send it.
askWorkstreamGoal.tip: Droid can only suggest a useful goal if it knows where new work shows up. Naming the source, such as a Slack channel, a Linear project or failing CI runs, lets it check what has really arrived there lately. A goal tied to a real source gives the workstream work on day one.

1.body: Pick a project you know for code-based goals, or an empty folder to talk about your team.

suggestWorkstreamGoals.title: 询问目标
suggestWorkstreamGoals.body: Pick a draft in the lesson panel, add your context, and send it.

projectGoals.title: 此项目的目标
projectGoals.description: Droid looks for work that keeps coming back.

action.text: Suggest up to three ongoing goals in this project that would make good workstreams, not one-off fixes. For each, say where new work shows up, one example change, and how we’d measure success. {{suggestOnly}}

Help me find an ongoing goal for a workstream. Ask what my team does, which problems keep coming back, and where we track them. Then suggest up to three goals and how we’d measure each. {{suggestOnly}}

createWorkstream.instructions: While Droid researches, check what you control. Setup asks for your approval at each stage.
createWorkstream.tip: Knowing what each approval allows keeps a workstream from doing more than you meant. Confirming the proposal saves a Draft without activating it, the test run saves results to the Draft without opening pull requests, and approval gates stay on with auto-merge off until you change them. Activate only after you read the test run.

tourWorkstreamsPage.summary: Find decisions, then start a Draft
tourWorkstreamsPage.instructions: Take one of Droid’s goals to the Workstreams page and select Create workstream.
tourWorkstreamsPage.tip: {{tourPanelTipPrefix}} Your Draft runs nothing until you activate it, so you can finish setup at your own pace. Activation turns on scheduled runs and the worker pool, and your approval gates and auto-merge setting stay as you left them.

tourWorkstreamList.title: 查看每个工作流
tourWorkstreamList.body: Each row counts its signals and changes. Open one to see its stages at work.

tourSoftwareFactoryInbox.title: 在收件箱中决策
tourSoftwareFactoryInbox.body: Changes and specs waiting for your approval collect here.

tourNewWorkstream.title: 创建草稿
tourNewWorkstream.body: Select Create workstream to save a Draft, then give Droid your goal. You approve every setup stage.
